story_type: heavy-lift helicopter carries a stealth fighter jet on a sling, over land and open water
hook: A stealth fighter, hanging from a helicopter.
narration: This is a stealth fighter, hanging under a helicopter.
It was the first F-35B ever built, and the first F-35 to land vertically.
In August 2025, the Marines moved it from Patuxent River, Maryland, to South Carolina.
The jet weighed twenty-two thousand pounds. The crew rigged it to a single hook.
A sling load swings like a pendulum, so the pilots fly slow and smooth, ready to release the hook in an emergency.
A second King Stallion flew along to refuel it on the ground.
Then the route went out over open water.
[short pause] A Marine commander said he had never heard of anyone moving one by helicopter.
The program manager said it finished the lift with power and range to spare.
outcome: The King Stallion delivered the jet to Marine Corps Air Station Beaufort, where it stays on permanent display.
title: F-35 slung under a helicopter
description:
On Aug. 27, 2025, a Marine CH-53K King Stallion from HMH-461 carried BF-1, the first F-35 to perform a vertical landing, from Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Maryland, to Marine Corps Air Station Beaufort, South Carolina, for a permanent static display.

Footage: U.S. Marine Corps video by Lance Cpl. Bryan Giraldo, 2nd Marine Aircraft Wing, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/975194/us-marines-with-marine-heavy-helicopter-squadron-hmh-461-transport-f-35b-lightning-ii-marine-corps-air-station-beaufort
